title: 1988 AHSME Problem 13
statement: If \(\sin x=3\cos x,\) then what is \(\sin x\cos x?\)

solutions.text:
Squaring gives \(\sin^2x=9\cos^2x.\) Hence \(10\cos^2x=1.\) Multiplying \(\sin x=3\cos x\) by \(\cos x\) gives \(\sin x\cos x=3\cos^2x=\frac{3}{10}.\)

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Square the given relation and use \(\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1\)
The given relation also determines the sign of the product
